Report ID: TR-001          Alert code: SYN-26-001A          Release date: 2026-09-14

# Credential-Phishing Campaign Delivering the "Larkspur" Loader

## ACTIONS TO TAKE TODAY
1. Search proxy and DNS logs for the network indicators in Table 1.
2. Isolate any endpoint that matches the file indicators in Table 2.
3. Reset credentials for users who submitted data to the phishing page.

## SUMMARY
Since late August 2026, a financially motivated actor tracked here as CINDER LYNX (fictional) has
sent invoice-themed phishing e-mails to staff in the logistics sector. Victims who open the
attachment are sent to a fake sign-in page and, in parallel, a small loader called Larkspur is
downloaded. Larkspur collects basic host information and polls a command-and-control (C2) server
for further payloads. Organisations should search their logs for the indicators below and treat any
match as a potential compromise.

## TECHNICAL DETAILS
### Initial Access
The e-mails carry an HTML attachment named like an invoice [T1566.001]. Opening it redirects the
browser to a credential-harvesting page hosted on login-portal-verify[.]example[.]com.
### Execution and Persistence
The same page triggers download of a script that installs Larkspur as a scheduled task
[T1053.005]. The loader binary is dropped as `svc_update.exe` in the user's AppData folder.
### Command and Control
Larkspur beacons every 10–15 minutes over HTTPS to cdn-sync[.]example[.]net [T1071.001]. Some
samples fall back to the raw IP address 203.0.113.45 when DNS resolution fails.

## INDICATORS OF COMPROMISE
Table 1: Malicious network indicators

| Indicator | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| login-portal-verify[.]example[.]com | Domain | Credential-harvesting page |
| cdn-sync[.]example[.]net | Domain | Larkspur C2 server |
| 203.0.113.45 | IPv4 | Fallback C2 address |

Table 2: File indicators

| File name | SHA-256 | Description |
|---|---|---|
| svc_update.exe | 4f1c9a0d7be35e2a81c6f09d3b47a5e8c2d6f1a09b3e7c45d8a2f6e1b0c9d374 | Larkspur loader |

## MITRE ATT&CK TECHNIQUES

| Technique Title | ID | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Phishing: Spearphishing Attachment | T1566.001 | Invoice-themed HTML attachment |
| Scheduled Task/Job: Scheduled Task | T1053.005 | Loader persistence |
| Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols | T1071.001 | HTTPS beaconing to C2 |

## DETECTION / HUNT RECOMMENDATIONS
- Search proxy logs for connections to the domains and IP address in Table 1.
- Search DNS logs for lookups of the domains in Table 1.
- Search EDR alerts for the SHA-256 hash in Table 2.

## MITIGATIONS
- E-mail: block HTML attachments from external senders; label external mail.
- Endpoint: alert on new scheduled tasks created from user-writable folders.
- Identity: enforce phishing-resistant MFA for web sign-in.

## REPORTING
Report matches to the fictional TRACE-RAG Synthetic Advisory Board contact channel.

## DISCLAIMER
This report is synthetic and was produced for research. All names, indicators, and events are
fictional. IP addresses come from RFC 5737 documentation ranges and domains from example.com,
example.net, and example.org.
